introH2: 🏘️ How many types of stay are there around the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: The Chanthaboon Riverside Community is a district of old wooden houses along the Chanthaburi River, running about 1 kilometre and packed with century-old wooden shophouses, old-school sweet shops, cafés, and a riverside way of life that's still very much alive — and the stays around it come in several styles to match your trip. Some are historic teakwood houses the community restored together until they earned a UNESCO award; some are budget-friendly old hotels that have stood with the town for over 60 years; some are riverside boutiques with a live-music bar in the evening; and some are small hostels where the owner looks after guests like friends. A lot of people come to Chanthaburi and end up picking a place that doesn't match their style, missing the charm of sleeping right in the old district. This article rounds up 5 stays around the Chanthaboon Riverside Community and Chanthaburi old town that we've reviewed in depth — riverside wooden houses, a downtown hotel, a riverside boutique, and hostels. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the good and the honest caveats, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Chanthaburi has no commercial airport in the province and no metro. Most people drive from Bangkok in about 3.5–4 hours, or take a minivan/coach to the Chanthaburi bus terminal and then a short ride into town. The areas covered in this article: Chanthaboon Riverside Community · Wat Mai sub-district — the old wooden-house district along the river, within walking distance of the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, Nam Phu Market, and all the food stalls. The streets are narrow and hard to drive into, so ask about parking spots in advance. Downtown · Benchamarachuthit / Si Chan Road — walking distance to the riverside community and the gem market, with easier parking. Chanthanimit — the east bank of the river; you can walk or cycle to the cathedral and the riverside community.

entries.name: Baan Luang Rajamaitri Historic Inn
entries.revCount: Real review score around 8.9 · from several hundred travellers · TripAdvisor #1 in the inn/guesthouse group in Chanthaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Heart of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community · 5-min walk to the cathedral
entries.addr: 252 Sukhaphiban Road, Wat Mai sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you had to pick one stay that best represents the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, most real reviews give it to this one — Baan Luang Rajamaitri Historic Inn (Baan Luang Rajamaitri) is no ordinary hotel. It's a teakwood house over 150 years old that belonged to Luang Rajamaitri (1876–1956), a nobleman-businessman who brought the first rubber trees into eastern Thailand. When the house fell into disrepair and was at risk of being torn down, more than 300 people from the community pooled their money to set up a community enterprise, bought it, and restored it as an inn so the income could flow back into caring for the old district — earning recognition from UNESCO in 2015 as a model for community-led conservation of an old town. The building is Sino-European architecture, with original teak floors and pillars and carved woodwork along the balcony railings, and it doubles as a museum, with antiques and photographs telling the community's story in every corner. What makes people fall in love is that all 12 rooms are decorated differently and named after episodes from Luang Rajamaitri's life — the Rubber Tree Room tells the rubber story, the Red and Green Gems Room tells the Chanthaburi gem story, all the way up to The Masters Room, the largest and most luxurious. What reviews agree on is the breakfast beside the Chanthaburi River, where you sit and watch boats and the slow current drift by, and staff so warm they feel like relatives, ready to tell the house's story and recommend spots around the community. The honest caveats from real reviews: it's an old house, the stairs are fairly steep and some doorways are low, so anyone with bad knees should take care; some rooms are compact; you take your shoes off and walk barefoot on the wooden floors as part of preserving the house; and the community streets are narrow, making it hard to drive right up to the inn — so ask about parking in advance. This isn't the option with a pool or wide modern rooms, but it's the best value for "a story" — for couples and history lovers who want to genuinely sleep inside the tale of Chanthaburi.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a river view or a view of the church spire, say so when you book, because the views differ room to room. Bring socks for walking barefoot on the wooden floors, and if you're travelling with elderly guests, ask for a ground-floor room first.

entries.name: Kasemsarn Hotel
entries.revCount: Booking.com around 8.4 · TripAdvisor around 4/5 · has stood with Chanthaburi for over 60 years
entries.badge: 💸 Best value in the group · free parking
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Downtown · Benchamarachuthit Road · 5-min walk to the Chanthaboon riverside
entries.addr: 98/1 Benchamarachuthit Road, Wat Mai sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi District
entries.storyHtml: Where the other Chanthaboon riverside stays in this article sell charm and design, Kasemsarn Hotel — which Chanthaburi locals know simply as Kasemsan Hotel — sells the most straightforward thing of all: a downtown location at the lightest price in the group. It's one of the longest-standing hotels in the town of Chanthaburi, open since 1961 and given a major renovation in 2006. The building is about 3 storeys with around 60 rooms, sitting on Benchamarachuthit Road in the centre of town. Its number-one selling point is a location just a few minutes' walk from the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, the old wooden-house district by the river, and a little further on to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, one of the largest and most beautiful churches in Thailand; Nam Phu Market, the well-known food spot, is about a 10-minute walk. Real reviews agree that the rooms are cleaner than the price suggests, the beds are comfortable, and the staff are friendly and helpful — many people are surprised the rooms are tidier than the building's exterior would suggest, and there's free parking and free Wi-Fi, with a 24-hour reception. Booking.com scores it around 8.4, rating it highly on value and amenities. The honest caveats from real reviews: the building is an older one with no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean stairs (staff often help with bags); some bathrooms are small with a tight shower area; some of the décor is starting to show its age; there's no pool; and rooms facing the road get some traffic noise. If you're after new-design rooms or a garden resort, this isn't the answer — but if you want the best-value base in the centre of town that's clean and makes exploring the old town easy, Kasemsarn does that job best in this article.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The building has no lift, so if you have heavy bags or find stairs difficult, ask for a ground-floor room when you book. If you want breakfast, choose a Deluxe room or higher, because some Standard rooms don't include breakfast.

entries.name: Tamajun Hotel
entries.revCount: Real review score around 8.2 · TripAdvisor #1 specialty lodging in Chanthaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Chanthaboon riverfront · 1-min walk to the heart of the community
entries.addr: 248 Sukhaphiban Road, Wat Mai sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi District
entries.storyHtml: Tamajun Hotel is a small boutique hotel of just 24 rooms that sits right in the heart of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community — ideal for people who want to sleep "in the old district" for real, not just wander through it and head back to sleep elsewhere. What makes it memorable is that it splits into two buildings with distinctly different characters — the HIP Hotel building is an old building renovated in a contemporary style with parquet floors, giving the feel of an old-town shophouse done up in a modern look, while the Tropical Thai Style side is a wooden house standing directly on the bank of the Chanthaboon River, with many rooms having balconies that jut out over the water, so you open the door to a view of the river and the community life on the opposite bank. The hotel is only about a 1-minute walk from the heart of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, and under 10 minutes' walk to Nam Phu Market, while the cathedral is just across Niramol Bridge. Another character people remember is the riverside bar with live music almost every night, which foreign reviews describe as "a really cool bar, river view, with live music," plus free bikes to borrow for exploring the old town, free breakfast, free Wi-Fi, and free parking. TripAdvisor ranks it #1 in the specialty-lodging group in Chanthaburi. The honest caveats, said plainly: the very thing that's the charm turns out to be the most common complaint — the live music plays until around midnight, and combined with the fairly thin walls of the old building, rooms near the bar hear the sound; some HIP-side rooms are fairly dark with no water view; the old building has no lift; and the breakfast menu is fairly limited. In short, it's the best value for "location and character" in the Chanthaboon Riverside Community — ideal for couples and photographers who want to wake up to the river and end the day with riverside music.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're here for the river view, ask specifically for a River View room on the Tropical Thai side; don't end up on the HIP side with no water view and some rooms fairly dark. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the bar or check which nights have live music before booking.
pros: Riverside rooms have balconies with views of the Chanthaboon River, and a vintage atmosphere that photographs beautifully
1-minute walk to the heart of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community · TripAdvisor #1 specialty lodging in Chanthaburi

entries.name: Chernchan Hostel
entries.revCount: Real review score around 9.0 · Trip.com around 9.0 · Booking.com at a similar level
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In town · Chanthanimit area · 7-min walk to the cathedral
tags: 🛏️ Almost all private rooms with en-suite bathroom
entries.addr: 43/11-13 Soi Trirat, Chanthanimit sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you think a hostel has to mean cramped bunk beds in a shared room with no privacy, Chernchan Hostel will change that picture. It's a small boutique hostel of about 19 rooms in the town of Chanthaburi, in the Chanthanimit area on the east bank of the Chanthaburi River, created from a major renovation of an existing building before opening in 2017. What sets it apart from a typical hostel is that it has just one shared dorm room, and nearly everything else is a private room with an en-suite bathroom — every room air-conditioned, with a flat-screen TV. The design throughout the building shows a care you rarely find at this price, from exposed-brick walls, framed paintings, and assorted globes to the shared lounge area laid with floor cushions, with a sofa, a guitar, and books for guests to come down and chat with other travellers. The location is a strength too — about a 7-minute walk to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception and Robinson department store, a little further across to the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, and there are free bikes to borrow that suit cycling around the old town and the riverside perfectly. Real reviews praise cleanliness as the standout, many using the words "spotlessly clean"; comfortable beds, friendly and helpful staff, and a Western-style breakfast that's tastier than expected push the real review score up to around 9.0, which is high for a stay at this level. The honest caveats from real reviews: rooms are fairly small, especially the cheapest no-window room, which feels cramped over several nights; the door locks in some rooms aren't very secure; the lift is small and tight, making it hard to move a large suitcase; and some reviews mention billing/deposit handling that occasionally stumbles. It's best for solo travellers, budget couples, and cyclists touring the old town who value cleanliness and design over room size.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Avoid the cheapest no-window room if you're staying several nights; paying a little more for a Deluxe or Twin with a window is much airier and more comfortable. Sort out the payment method and deposit clearly when you book or check in.

entries.name: Traveller Hostel Chanthaburi
entries.revCount: Real review score around 9.6 · Booking.com around 9.6 · Agoda around 9.5 · almost all reviews positive
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town · Si Chan Road · 2-min walk to the gem market
tags: 🧑‍✈️ Run by an owner who's a former guide
✨ So clean and quiet you sleep soundly
entries.addr: 3/2 Si Chan Road, Wat Mai sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi District
entries.storyHtml: Where the other hostels in this article sell design or a riverside location, Traveller Hostel Chanthaburi sells the hardest thing to put a number on — the close, personal care of its owner. It's a small boutique hostel of just 7 rooms on Si Chan Road in the heart of Chanthaburi old town, near the foot of the bridge and the gem market. What every review agrees on is that the owner, Peter, a former guide from Bangkok who speaks fluent English, looks after guests himself — recommending routes, pointing out which restaurants the locals actually eat at, when the market is busiest, even helping arrange private trips at times, to the point that many foreign reviews agree it "feels like having a local friend looking out for you." The location is a strength too — about a 2-minute walk to the gem market, around 5–10 minutes across the bridge to the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, and the cathedral is about a 5–7 minute walk or a short cycle away. The most praised point across every platform is cleanliness, scoring nearly full marks — fresh linens, bathroom amenities better than a hostel's price would suggest — and the quiet that many say lets them sleep soundly all night, which is rare for a stay in the centre of town. There's free high-speed Wi-Fi, a lounge with free drinking water, tea, and coffee, laundry service, and bike rental, and the price starting around ฿350/night is the lightest starting point in this article. The honest caveats from real reviews: it's a small hostel with just 7 rooms and fills up fast over long weekends, so book ahead; there's no pool, gym, or hotel-style amenities; private parking is limited because it's on a narrow street; and at times it's noted as adults-only. It's best for solo travellers and budget couples who plan to explore the old town and the Chanthaboon Riverside Community and want someone to tell them the stories of Chanthaburi.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Always book ahead, because there are only 7 rooms and they fill up fast, especially Friday–Sunday when the gem market is busy. Once you check in, try asking Peter about local restaurants and walking routes around the old town — this is the kind of thing you won't find in an app.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about Chanthaboon riverside stays in Chanthaburi

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best stay around the Chanthaboon Riverside Community?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. If you want the most historic atmosphere, Baan Luang Rajamaitri Historic Inn, a 150-year-old teakwood house with a UNESCO award in the heart of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, score around 8.9. If you want the best-value base in the centre of town, Kasemsarn Hotel from ฿900. If you want to sleep by the river with a live-music bar, Tamajun Hotel. If you're after design on a budget, Chernchan Hostel with a score around 9. And if you want a local owner looking after you at the lightest price, Traveller Hostel with a score around 9.6.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chanthaboon riverside stays cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at around ฿350–1,500 per night. At the lightest end are Traveller Hostel from ฿350 and Chernchan Hostel from ฿700. Downtown hotels like Kasemsarn start at ฿900. The riverside boutique Tamajun starts at ฿1,200. And the historic wooden house Baan Luang Rajamaitri starts at ฿1,500 (up to around ฿3,500 for the largest room). All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard rooms, and may be higher than usual during festivals and the fruit season.

faq.q: ❓ What is the Chanthaboon Riverside Community · how close are the stays?
faq.a: The Chanthaboon Riverside Community is a district of old wooden houses along the Chanthaburi River, running about 1 kilometre and packed with century-old wooden shophouses, old-school sweet shops, cafés, and a riverside way of life that's still alive. In this article, Baan Luang Rajamaitri and Tamajun are right in the middle of the district (a 1–5 minute walk to the key spots), while Kasemsarn is about a 5-minute walk, Traveller Hostel is about 5–10 minutes across the bridge, and Chernchan is on the Chanthanimit side within walking distance. Nearly every one is within walking distance of the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, the town's landmark.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chanthaboon riverside stay suits couples?
faq.a: The stays that stand out most for a couple's atmosphere are Baan Luang Rajamaitri Historic Inn, a riverside wooden house that photographs beautifully from every angle and has The Masters Room for special occasions, and Tamajun Hotel, with riverside rooms with lovely views and a live-music bar in the evening. For budget couples who want a clean, design-led private room, Chernchan Hostel is also a good choice at a lighter price.

faq.q: ❓ Driving to Chanthaburi — which stay has convenient parking?
faq.a: If you're driving and parking matters to you, Kasemsarn Hotel has free in-hotel parking and sits on a main road, so you can park and then walk around the old town. The stays in the heart of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community like Baan Luang Rajamaitri and Tamajun are on narrow streets that are hard to drive into, so ask about parking in advance and be ready to wheel your bags in on foot. Chernchan and Traveller Hostel use nearby public parking.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Chanthaboon riverside stay?
faq.a: Most stays in this article are old houses or small hostels (7–24 rooms, some just 7 rooms), so they fill up fast. During the Chanthaburi fruit festival (around May–June) and long weekends, book several weeks ahead, especially Baan Luang Rajamaitri and Traveller Hostel, which have very few rooms. Other times, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. We recommend choosing Free Cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
